messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: Pager fired: runtime-canary.healthcheck: 5xx spike during canary rollout. PagerID pd_8a3f.

pagerduty-bot: PagerDuty alert triggered — escalation policy: runtime-canary-team. Triggered at 2154321987.

Samir (eng-oncall): ack'ed. I'm on call — taking primary. Anyone with recent canary context?

Rachel (deploy): noted. Pushed canary for release v1.12.4 ~ 30m ago. Canary traffic was 5% -> 20% ramp scheduled. I saw a small increase in failures on the first 10min.

Leo (sre): seeing healthcheck 502/504s from the canary group across 3 AZs. Logs show backend worker timeouts on page generation. P99 latency jumped ~900ms -> 6s.

Samir (eng-oncall): that's bad. Can we throttle canary traffic back to 0% while we triage? Rachel can you stop the ramp?

Rachel (deploy): doing now. Running rollback-hook to freeze traffic.

deploy-bot: Running command: `redwood deploy traffic set runtime-canary --percent 0 --selector canary=v1.12.4`

deploy-bot: Command output:
```
Scaling traffic: from 20% -> 0%
Updating routing entries...
Done. Active traffic redistributed to stable (v1.12.3).
```

Samir (eng-oncall): confirmed traffic is back to stable. Telemetry p95/p99 back near normal.

Leo (sre): customer-facing errors dropped after diversion. No active customer incidents reported yet. Alice can you check product for any alerts from customers?

Alice (product): checked support queue — 2 tickets flagged with transient failures in the last 25min, both from internal customers using heavy-batch endpoints. Marking severity: medium; no outage declared. I'll draft a note if we need proactive comms.

Samir (eng-oncall): good catch. We need a mitigation plan and a root cause hypothesis before re-ramping. Initial ask: grab a few failing request traces from canary pods. Leo, can you pull tail of logs + stack traces?

Leo (sre): pulling logs from canary pods (pod names redacted):
```
2026-03-15T12:05:37Z runtime-canary-7f5b cpu=78% mem=62% call_id=abc123 elapsed=5582ms status=timeout
2026-03-15T12:06:01Z runtime-canary-3c2a cpu=85% mem=69% call_id=def456 elapsed=6130ms status=timeout
2026-03-15T12:06:23Z runtime-canary-9b8d cpu=90% mem=74% call_id=ghi789 elapsed=7251ms status=oom-protect
```
Looks like a resource spike + occasional OOM-protect throttle on the canary binary.

Rachel (deploy): canary pods were using the new tokenization path (quantized tokenizer v2) in this release. We suspected it might be slightly heavier. Did we change memory limits? I thought we left limits same as stable.

Samir (eng-oncall): check container limits and JVM/native heap settings.

Leo (sre): checking k8s config now:
```
kubectl get deploy runtime-canary -o yaml | egrep "memory|cpu|args" -n
resources:
  limits:
    cpu: "2000m"
    memory: "6Gi"
  requests:
    cpu: "500m"
    memory: "2Gi"
```
Stable has 8Gi limit. Canary somehow got 6Gi. That mismatch would explain OOM-protects under higher concurrency.

Rachel (deploy): ugh, that's on me — my canary manifest for v1.12.4 used an old template. I'm rolling a patch to align limits with stable. Can do a reversible update if we want to re-ramp slowly.

Samir (eng-oncall): priority one: keep traffic on stable. Priority two: confirm resource parity, run a canary with 100% resource parity but keep traffic at 5% for a sanity test. Rachel, patch and create a controlled small ramp. Also add liveness probes to catch early.

Rachel (deploy): patch created, PR #4129. I'll apply to canary namespace now with a quick deploy: `kubectl apply -f canary-resources-patch.yaml`

deploy-bot: Applying patch...
```
deployment.apps/runtime-canary patched
rolling update started
pods updated: 3/3
```

Leo (sre): new pods up and warm. Memory limits now 8Gi matching stable. Monitoring heap profiles and KV cache consumption.

Samir (eng-oncall): recommend leaving traffic at 0% for 10 minutes, then ramp to 1% for 5 minutes, watch p95/5xx. Rachel, coordinate the ramp and keep me posted. If any 5xx spike > baseline+2% -> immediate rollback.

Rachel (deploy): ack. Scheduling incremental ramp: 0->1% now.

deploy-bot: Command: `redwood deploy traffic set runtime-canary --percent 1 --selector canary=v1.12.4`

deploy-bot: Output: traffic set to 1%

Leo (sre): watching metrics... p95 stable. No increased 5xx so far. Memory use looks steady.

Samir (eng-oncall): good sign. Keep slow ramping. Next step 1->5% in 10min if stable.

Alice (product): support queue cleared the two tickets with 'working again' notes. I'll add a short postmortem note to the customer ops doc once we conclude.

Rachel (deploy): noting remediation steps in the deploy ticket. Root cause hypothesis: resource limit mismatch from stale canary manifest + heavier quantized tokenizer path. Action items: 1) fix manifest templates, 2) add a pre-rollout check to compare stable vs canary resource configs, 3) add a short canary-only load test before ramp.

Samir (eng-oncall): agreed. Also add an automated lint in CI that fails if resource limits differ by >10% from stable for runtime services.

Leo (sre): I'll open SRE follow-up to add alert for OOM-protect spikes and CPU throttling during rollouts.

Rachel (deploy): ramping to 5% now as planned.

deploy-bot: traffic update to 5% complete.

Leo (sre): monitoring... slight p99 blip on one AZ but stabilized quickly. No customer error rate increase.

Samir (eng-oncall): keep watch for 30m. If all good, we can continue the rollout. For now incident marked 'mitigated' — root cause and follow-ups assigned.

Samir (eng-oncall): who will own the postmortem? Rachel, can you own the deploy side? Leo you own SRE alerts follow-up. I'll own the incident timeline + pager review.

Rachel (deploy): taking postmortem (PR/notes) and template fixes.

Leo (sre): taking alerting work.

OpsRotation: thx all. I'll update oncall rotation notes with the quick mitigation steps we ran.

incident-bot: Incident state changed: mitigated -> under-review. Pager auto-resolved at 2154322300.

Samir (eng-oncall): closing thread for now, will re-open if we see regression. Great cross-team response. :thumbsup:
